results.label: thm_geom
results.title: Maximal discrepancy under closure: l^T(closure omega) <= (1/2)(l^T(interior omega)+1) for C^2 metrics and C^1-type omega

proof.kind: prose proof in Section 2.2 with two embedded lemma proofs

results.notes: Statement is self-contained; assumptions (i) metric at least C^2, (ii) omega embedded C^1 submanifold with boundary if dim M>=3 and piecewise C^1 if dim M=2 are inside the theorem environment as enumeratei items 144-147. No proof environment for the theorem itself: the argument is prose 315-415, relying on Lemma 1 (existence of a minimizing ray) and Lemma 2 (two-sided transverse perturbation of a grazing ray).

results.label: cor_geom
results.title: Under Theorem 1 assumptions, l^T(closure omega)>1/2 implies l^T(interior omega)>0 and C_T(omega)>0
results.notes: Derivation: Theorem 1 gives l^T(interior omega) >= 2 l^T(closure omega) - 1 > 0; observability on the open set interior omega is cited (GCC, line 127). No independent new mechanism.

results.label: thm_random
results.title: Convergence in probability of l^T(omega_epsilon^n) to epsilon for random checkerboards on the flat torus

proof.kind: prose proof, Section 3 (with Lemmas 3-6, Proposition 1 and two auxiliary lemmas)

results.notes: Statement depends on the construction of omega_epsilon^n (lines 176-203, outside the theorem environment). Proof splits into (igd1) via Tchebyshev and (igd2) via Lemmas 4-6 plus the large deviation Proposition 1.

results.title: Probability that the wave equation on the torus is observable on omega_epsilon^n in time T tends to 1 as n -> infinity

proof.kind: prose combination of Theorem 2 with a cited result

results.notes: The derivation 212-217 combines Theorem 2 with the checkerboard observability criterion of [Burq2017, BurqGerard2018] (external; bibliography file missing). Not an author-complete new proof.

results.label: cor_optimforme
results.title: sup over |omega| <= epsilon (Lipschitz boundary) of l^T(omega) equals epsilon on the flat torus
results.notes: Uses Theorem 2 with epsilon' = epsilon - delta plus the cited inequality l^T(omega) <= |omega| of [HebrardHumbert] (line 1021). Short derivation; no new mechanism.

results.label: remgen
results.title: Weakenings of regularity assumption (ii): piecewise C^1 stratified sets in dimension 2; singleton-subdifferential criterion for boundary sections

proof.kind: none in the remark; retrospective assertion at 384-385

results.notes: The claim that the Lemma 2 argument 'still works' under the subdifferential-singleton hypothesis (385) is asserted, not separately proved.

results.label: lemma1
results.title: The infimum defining l^T(omega) is attained by some geodesic ray
results.notes: Compactness of geodesics + Fatou; the same argument reappears as Lemma 11 (lemg2open, 1187-1201).

results.label: lemma2
results.title: Existence of a continuous path s -> x_s through x_0 such that the rays gamma_s, gamma_-s lie on opposite sides a.e. on {gamma in boundary omega}
results.notes: The load-bearing new geometric mechanism of Theorem 1: local extremal-field coordinates along gamma (352-355), reduction to the tangency set Omega (363-368), and a projective-space Fubini argument producing V with <V,v(t)> != 0 for a.e. t in Omega (370-381). Uses the classical extremal-field construction cited to [Berger] (352-353) and the standard fact that conjugate times are isolated (footnote 354).

results.label: lem3hv
results.title: Upper semicontinuity of gamma -> m^T_gamma(omega) for closed omega; continuity at non-horizontal/non-vertical rays, or horizontal/vertical rays avoiding corners, for omega a union of closed grid cells
results.notes: Dominated convergence and a finite boundary-crossing count (461). Used inside Theorem 2's comparison lemma.

results.title: Standalone braced block defining tilde m^T_gamma(omega) by a liminf over rays obtained by rotating gamma around a grid corner
results.notes: Not inside a definition environment. Introduces the quantity used for horizontal/vertical rays through corners; inequality l^T <= tilde m <= m stated at 471.

results.label: lem:smallT
results.title: If (igd2) holds for every T in (0,1) then it holds for every T>0
results.notes: Monotonicity l^T >= l^{T'} with T' = T/m; also yields that for 0<T<1 a ray crosses a given cell at most once (534-535).

results.label: lem:compare
results.title: Two quantitative comparisons: l^T_{Gamma^1} <= l^T + C/n and l^T_{Gamma^2} <= l^T_{Gamma^1} + C/n, uniformly over cell-unions of the n-grid
results.notes: Item (a): translation of the ray and affine cell-crossing weights (604-637). Item (b): rotation about the single grid corner, explicit crossing-time formula t^n_ij(theta)=a_ij/(n sin)+b_ij/(n cos) (689-715), minimization of X_1/sin+X_2/cos (740-783), angle bounds (756-759). This is the new quantitative stability estimate controlling near-tangent and corner-hitting rays.

results.label: lem:limprobg4
results.title: P(l^T_{Gamma^2}(omega_epsilon^n) <= epsilon - delta) -> 0
results.notes: Equivalence classes hat Gamma determined by two distinct cells and two distinct corners, #hat Gamma = O(n^8) (792-794); Chernoff bound uniform over each class with m >= nT/sqrt(2) cells (797-833); union bound giving n^9 exp(-2nT^2 delta^2/(9(T+1))) (847-851). Horizontal/vertical classes go through tilde m and at most 2 floor(n/T)+2 limit points (806-825).

results.label: prop:largeDev
results.title: Large deviation bound P(|Y_m - epsilon| >= delta) <= C_{epsilon,delta} exp(-delta^2 m / c) for weighted i.i.d. Bernoulli sums with lambda_i <= c/m

proof.kind: proof environment containing two auxiliary lemmas

results.notes: Presented in the text as 'one of the main ingredients of the proof of Theorem 2' (line 424) and used twice (non-horizontal classes 797-800; limit points of horizontal/vertical classes 814-820). The proof is self-contained (Chernoff/Markov bound, optimization over the simplex Sigma_m, choice of s), but the statement is a tool for Theorem 2, so not counted as a separate core.

results.title: The restrictions c>1 and m>=3 are not restrictive and allow a sharp estimate via an auxiliary optimization problem
results.notes: Comment on Proposition 1.

results.label: lem:auxRes
results.title: Exact value of max over Sigma_m of the product F (extremal configuration: floor(m/c) coordinates at c/m, one leftover, rest zero)
results.notes: Auxiliary optimization for Proposition 1: pairwise perturbation, a Hessian/eigenvalue count (926-927), then monotonicity of phi (942-947).

results.label: lem:estim1214
results.title: Case analysis for phi_{epsilon,delta}(u) = u(epsilon+delta) - log(1-epsilon+epsilon e^u): existence of hat u with phi = delta^2 and explicit upper bounds U_{epsilon,delta}
results.notes: Auxiliary calculus for the choice s = hat u_{epsilon,delta}/c in Proposition 1.

results.label: remEgorov
results.title: Egorov-type symbolic interpretation of a_t = a o phi_t for a principal symbol a in C^infty(S^*M)
results.notes: Uses the Egorov theorem cited to [Zworski] (bibliography missing). Context for the microlocal interpretation 1076-1115, which contains no theorem environment.

results.label: lemBorel
results.title: If bounded Borel h_k -> chi_omega pointwise then limsup l^T(h_k) <= l^T(omega); if moreover chi_omega <= h_k then equality with the infimum over k
results.notes: Appendix material 'for completeness' (line 159). Dominated convergence; the text stresses at 1138 that a.e. convergence would not suffice.

results.label: rem_openclosed
results.title: Characterization of open/closed subsets by monotone sequences of continuous functions below/above chi_omega
results.notes: Elementary distance-function constructions; supports the hypothesis of Lemma 10.

results.label: lemopen
results.title: For open omega and continuous h_k increasing pointwise to chi_omega, l^T(omega) = lim l^T(h_k) = sup_k l^T(h_k)
results.notes: Compactness of geodesics, Dini's theorem on a compact neighbourhood, Fatou. Appendix material.

results.title: Lemmas 9 and 10 remain valid for subsets of S^*M
results.notes: One-sentence observation.

results.label: lemg2open
results.title: For open omega the infimum defining l^T(omega) is attained
results.notes: Repeats the argument of Lemma 1 ('almost contained in the proof of Lemma 10'). Appendix completeness material.
